message_bot.description: DM another Bot for help. It works in its private chat; the reply returns here and you continue

params.text: What it should do — complete and self-contained (it cannot see this chat)

handoff.description: In a group, hand work to another Bot — it continues immediately

params.request: What it should do — complete (it can see prior group messages)

params.handoff_to: Group only: which member should continue after the task
params.handoff_note: What the next Bot should do on handoff

save_skill.description: Save or overwrite a skill (reusable procedure)

params.name: Short name for /name, no spaces
params.description: One line on when to use it
params.body: Full procedure: steps, sites/apps, output format

params.name: Name; webhook names: letters, digits, - _ only
params.prompt: What to do each run — complete
params.skill: Optional skill to follow each run (no leading /)

remember.description: Store a long-term memory (carried into later chats)

params.text: One complete sentence, e.g. “user wants conclusions first”
params.shared: Basic facts about the user (name, timezone, city…) = true, shared by all Bots
params.replace_id: Optional: replace an existing memory id

params.note: Optional user note, e.g. change requests
params.always: true if the user said to stop asking for similar ops

recall.description: Fetch an earlier message by id

look_at_screen.description: Glance at the shared computer screen (screenshot + window title). Use when asked what’s on screen, where a task is, or what to dispatch next. View only — dispatch to act.

browser_open.description: Open a URL in the computer browser (current tab); returns numbered actionable elements and page text start

browser_snapshot.description: Inspect the current browser page: numbered elements [n], text start, scroll position. Use when the page changed or you are unsure.

browser_click.description: Click a page element; ref is the index from browser_snapshot

browser_type.description: Type into an input (clears existing text first). ref is the input index; submit=true presses Enter after typing.

browser_key.description: Press one key on the page: Enter, Tab, Escape, Backspace, ArrowDown, ArrowUp, PageDown, etc.

browser_scroll.description: Scroll the page by one screen

browser_read.description: Read the full text of the current page (up to 12000 chars per call; use offset to continue)

computer_screenshot.description: Capture the computer screen as an image. Use to see visuals (images, charts, layout, captchas); for page text/elements use browser_snapshot.

computer_click.description: [Fallback] Click screen coordinates (x, y). Only when browser_click cannot (non-browser windows, canvas).

computer_type.description: [Fallback] Type at the current focus. For web inputs use browser_type

computer_key.description: Press a key or chord, e.g. Enter, Tab, ctrl+l, ctrl+a, Escape

computer_scroll.description: [Fallback] Scroll at the mouse position. For web use browser_scroll

computer_shell.description: Run a bash command on the computer terminal (cwd /data/workspace; files persist). Good for downloads, data processing, scripts.

computer_read_file.description: Read a text file on the computer

computer_write_file.description: Write a text file on the computer (overwrites)

ask_human.description: Call for human-only steps (login, captcha, QR scan, payment verification, choices the user must make): the user takes the computer, then hands it back. State clearly what they should do.

ask_approval.description: Call before consequential actions: submit forms, place orders/pay, send messages/email, delete data, publish. State the action and impact. Continue only after the user agrees.
